newsitem.title: UK: British bankers welcome BOE supervision proposals.
newsitem.headline: British bankers welcome BOE supervision proposals.

text.p: The British Bankers' Association on Monday welcomed proposals from the Bank of England which will move banking supervision to a more risk-based regime, adding that the quality of supervision is more important than its quantity.

"Any new supervisory regime should be able to distinguish between different kinds of banking organisation whilst avoiding any unnecessary increase in the burden of supervision," said Tim Sweeney, director-general of the BBA.
The amount of senior management time, the attendant costs of this and the use of external advisers concerned with supervision, have been the cause of increasing concern within the banking community.
The Bank of England earlier launched the new regulatory framework, which would take more account of individual risk situations and risk controls.
The Bank said it will identify "significant" business units and look at these closely as well as looking at an institution as a whole.

The proposals follow the BOE's Review of Banking Supervision published last year, which came as a direct result of a report by consultants Arthur Andersen into the supervisory ramifications of the collapse of investment bank Barings in February 1995.
The BBA said it will examine the plausibility of today's proposals and their impact in terms of prudential effectiveness and cost.
It welcomed the fact that "higher risk" operations will receive more and clearer supervision focused on the high risk areas.
The BBA said it hoped the BOE's claim that little additional information will be required from banks will indeed be the case.
